items.readable_text:
Content:
Suppose that we want to solve the equation
[MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}x = 8.]

Content:
This equation has a fractional coefficient of [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}.] The term [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}x] means that [MATH: x] is being multiplied by [MATH: 2] and divided by [MATH: 3.]

Content:
We can solve this problem by applying the multiplication principle, twice. First, we multiply both sides by [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] to get rid of the fraction:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{2}{3}x &= 8 \[5pt]
{\color{blue}{3}}\cdot \dfrac{2}{3}x &={\color{blue}{3}}\cdot 8 \[5pt]
\cancel{\color{blue}{3}} \cdot \dfrac{2}{\cancel{3}}x &={\color{blue}{3}}\cdot 8 \
2x &=24
}]

Content:
Then, we divide both sides by [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}] to isolate [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
2x &=24\[5pt]
\dfrac{2x}{{\color{red}{2}}} &=\dfrac{24}{{\color{red}{2}}} \[5pt]
\dfrac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{\color{red}{2}}} &=\dfrac{24}{{\color{red}{2}}} \
x &=12
}]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac{3x}{4}-5 &=-8\[5pt] \dfrac{3x}{4}-5+5 &=-8+5\[5pt] \dfrac{3x}{4}+0 &=-3 \[5pt] \dfrac{3x}{4} &=-3 }]

[MATH: \eqalign{ \dfrac{3}{4}x &=-3 \[5pt] \dfrac{4}{3} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4}x &= \dfrac{4}{3} \cdot (-3) \[5pt] 1 x &= - \dfrac{4}{\cancel{3} } \cdot \cancel{3} \[5pt] x &= -4. }]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Suppose that we want to solve the equation
[MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}x = 8.]

Content:
This equation has a fractional coefficient of [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}.] The term [MATH: \dfrac{2}{3}x] means that [MATH: x] is being multiplied by [MATH: 2] and divided by [MATH: 3.]

Content:
We can solve this problem by applying the multiplication principle, twice. First, we multiply both sides by [MATH: {\color{blue}{3}}] to get rid of the fraction:

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{2}{3}x &= 8 \[5pt]
{\color{blue}{3}}\cdot \dfrac{2}{3}x &={\color{blue}{3}}\cdot 8 \[5pt]
\cancel{\color{blue}{3}} \cdot \dfrac{2}{\cancel{3}}x &={\color{blue}{3}}\cdot 8 \
2x &=24
}]

Content:
Then, we divide both sides by [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}] to isolate [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \eqalign{
2x &=24\[5pt]
\dfrac{2x}{{\color{red}{2}}} &=\dfrac{24}{{\color{red}{2}}} \[5pt]
\dfrac{\cancel{2}x}{\cancel{\color{red}{2}}} &=\dfrac{24}{{\color{red}{2}}} \
x &=12
}]

---

Item 2 — Example: Solving One-Step Linear Equations Without the Reciprocal

Example Prompt:
Solve for [MATH: x,] if [MATH: -\dfrac{3}{4}x = 12.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we multiply both sides by [MATH: \color{blue}4] to get rid of the fraction:

[MATH: − (3)/(4)x|= 12; 4 ⋅ (− (3)/(4)x)|= 4 ⋅ 12; 4 ⋅ (− (3)/(4)x)|= 48; − 3x|= 48]

Then, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: {\color{red}-3}] to isolate [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

[MATH: − 3x|= 48; (− 3x)/(− 3)|= (48)/(− 3); (− 3x)/(− 3)|= − 16; x|= − 16]

Item 5 — Tutorial: Using the Reciprocal

Content:
When solving equations with fractional coefficients, there is a shortcut! We can complete division and multiplication in a single step by multiplying both sides of the equation by the reciprocal of the fractional coefficient.

Content:
For example, to solve the equation [MATH: \dfrac{2x}{5}= 6,] we first express the fraction as a coefficient:

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
\eqalign{
\dfrac{2}{5}x &= 6
}]

Content:
The fractional coefficient is [MATH: \dfrac{2}{5}], and its reciprocal is [MATH: \left(\dfrac 2 5\right)^{-1} = {\color{blue}{\dfrac 5 2}}.] Because the product of a fraction and its reciprocal is equal to [MATH: 1,] we can multiply both sides of the equation by the reciprocal to isolate [MATH: x\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \require{cancel}
\eqalign{
\dfrac{2}{5}x &= 6 \[5pt]
\underbrace{ {\color{blue}{\dfrac 5 2}} \cdot \dfrac{2}{5} }_{\large =\, 1} x &= {\color{blue}{\dfrac 5 2}} \cdot 6 \[5pt]
1 x &= \dfrac{5\cdot 6}{2} \[5pt]
x &= \dfrac{30}{2} \[5pt]

x &= 15
}]

---

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We multiply both sides of the equation by the reciprocal of [MATH: -\dfrac{3}{2},] which is [MATH: \left( -\dfrac{3}{2} \right)^{-1} = -\dfrac{2}{3}.] This gives
[MATH: − (3)/(2)t|= 24; − (2)/(3) ⋅ (− (3)/(2)t)|= − (2)/(3) ⋅ 24; 1t|= − (2)/(3) ⋅ 3 ⋅ 8; t|= − 16.]

Item 9 — Example: Solving Two-Step Linear Equations With the Reciprocal

Example Prompt:
Solve the equation [MATH: \dfrac{3x}{4}-5 = -8.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we isolate the fractional term [MATH: \dfrac{3x}{4}] by adding [MATH: 5] to both sides:

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{3x}{4}-5 &=-8\[5pt]
\dfrac{3x}{4}-5+5 &=-8+5\[5pt]
\dfrac{3x}{4}+0 &=-3 \[5pt]
\dfrac{3x}{4} &=-3
}]

The fractional coefficient is [MATH: \dfrac{3}{4},] so we multiply by its reciprocal [MATH: \left( \dfrac{3}{4} \right)^{-1} = \dfrac{4}{3}.] This gives

[MATH: \eqalign{
\dfrac{3}{4}x &=-3 \[5pt]
\dfrac{4}{3} \cdot \dfrac{3}{4}x &= \dfrac{4}{3} \cdot (-3) \[5pt]
1 x &= - \dfrac{4}{\cancel{3} } \cdot \cancel{3} \[5pt]
x &= -4.
}]
